sentences.text: The allegation against the petitioner is that he has raped the prosecutrix who is already married.
It is 1 Whether reporters of Local Papers may be allowed to see the judgment?

Yes. 
alleged that prosecutrix had acquaintance with the petitioner as both were studying in the same educational .
institute.
Prosecutrix was married on 27th September, 2022.

She has alleged that on 1st November,
2022 the petitioner met her in the college and threatened her to black male on the basis of her photographs and telephonic chat available with him.
It is further alleged that the prosecutrix under such threat, accompanied the petitioner to a hotel where she was raped more than once against her wish.
Thereafter, as per prosecutrix, the petitioner hired auto rikshaw and brought the prosecutrix to bus stand Mandi and from there both of them boarded a bus to reach Ner Chowk.
3. Petitioner was arrested on 3rd November, 2022 and is in custody since then.
4. Petitioner has made a prayer for grant of bail on the ground that the allegations leveled against him are false.

The prosecutrix had accompanied the petitioner of her own will and whatever had _________________________________________________ vs State Of H.P on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5084155/
1 happened was with the consent of the prosecutrix.
It has further been contended that the allegations with respect to threat of black male etc are concocted.
As per petitioner till date no legal evidence is against him.
The investigation has been completed and challan stands filed in the Court.

Petitioner is stated to be .
permanent resident of Village and Post Office Meramsit Tehsil Balh, District Mandi, H.P.
He has undertaken to abide by all the terms and conditions as may be imposed.
5. Per contra, learned Deputy Advocate General has opposed the bail application on the ground that the offence charged against petitioner is of a serious nature.
It has further been submitted that in case of release of petitioner on bail, he may tamper with the prosecution evidence.
6. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and have also gone through the case file carefully.
7. Prosecutrix is aged about 20 years.
It is not denied that the prosecutrix had prior acquaintance with the petitioner.
From the bare allegations leveled by the prosecutrix, it appears that she was intimately known to petitioner before her marriage.

Though, at the stage of deciding the bail application, this Court will not venture into the detailed analysis of the material collected by Investigating Agency, yet the same need to be looked into only for the purpose of adjudging the seriousness and gravity of offence against the petitioner.

. 
8. Even after the alleged offence, the prosecutrix had travelled firstly to bus stand Mandi and thereafter to Ner Chowk with petitioner without any objection, is a fact which needs to be noticed.
The allegation against petitioner is yet to be proved.
Pre-trial incarceration cannot be ordered as a matter of rule.
The investigation stands completed and challan has already been filed.
In such circumstances, no fruitful purpose shall be served by prolonging the pre-trial incarceration of the petitioner.
9. Petitioner is permanent resident of VPO Meramsit Tehsil Balh, District Mandi, H.P. and there is no likelihood on his absconding from course of justice.
The apprehension expressed on behalf of the respondent that the petitioner may tamper with the prosecution evidence can be taken care of by putting the petitioner to appropriate terms.

10. In view of peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, petition is allowed and the petitioner is ordered to be released on bail in case FIR No.43 of 2022, under Sections 376(2) (n) (h) and 506 of Indian Penal Code, registered at Women Police Station Mandi, District Mandi, H.P. on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.
.
25,000/- with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of learned trial Court.
